text:
maria: heads-up — bringing novaX-7B (converted from hf) up on dedicated-int4. baseline ppl looks ok but enabling our rotary_adapter produces subtle hallucination regressions and token aliasing in long context.

jin: can you paste a tiny repro? sample inputs + model outputs?

maria: repro below (shortened). note tokens around <|end|> shift: 
```
input: 'Summarize the release notes for 2026-03-15'
tokens (hf): [50256, 345, 12, 78, 50256]
model out (no adapter): 'Release notes: ...'
model out (adapter + int4): '
Release notes: 
1. Fixed latency.
2. New API.'  <-- repeats and adds extraneous list items
```

ashok: hmm repeating + extra bullets often points to rotary misalignment or kv-cache token-id offset. did the tokenizer conversion script change bos/eos ids or add sentinels?

maria: converter left sentinel tokens at same indices AFAICT. but we did run `token-normalizer --nfkc` during conversion.

olga: quick check: do embeddings between hf and converted match for first token? run: `python -c "print(model.embed(torch.tensor([50256])))"`

maria: ran that — vectors differ by ~1e-3 (should be <1e-5). attaching small dump in case: `embed0_hf != embed0_converted`

jin: that magnitude suggests a remap or byte-order/endianness during weight save or a layout transpose. also adapter code injects per-head rotary scaling — if head ordering differs between hf and runtime that could warp angles.

ashok: bisect suggestion: 1) run float32 converted model (no quant) + adapter 2) run int4 without adapter 3) run int4 with adapter. that isolates quant vs adapter.

maria: did steps: float32+adapter = ok, int4 w/o adapter = ok, int4+adapter = bad. so interaction with quantization and adapter logic.

jin: helpful. next try: disable headwise-rotary-scaling in adapter (turn off per-head scale) and retry. if fixed, we know it's head-order/scale-related.

olga: also check tokenizer special tokens mapping — sometimes `pad` got remapped to eos index during byte-conversion. run quick token checks: `for t in [bos,eos,pad]: print(t, tok.decode([t]))`.

maria: ran token checks — pad/eos/bos map fine. i'll run jin's disabled-scale test now.

ci-bot: perf test queued: run_id=mr-6012345678-01, endpoints: dedicated-int4, samples=500, metrics=[ppl, repeat-rate, latency_p50]. link: https://ci.redwood/tests/mr-6012345678-01

ashok: if disabling scale fixes it, we should then try switching adapter to use head-indexed permutation used in hf (we had a legacy reorder step in loader). may be a one-off head-permutation bug.

maria: result: disabling per-head scale -> behavior returns to baseline. int4+adapter now matches float32 baseline on the 50 test prompts.

jin: ok that nails headwise-scaling interaction with int4 kernels. likely quant rounding amplified small head-order mismatch into decoding errors.

olga: plan: 1) open bug for loader head-order + add unit test that compares headwise rotary bases between hf and runtime 2) add optional runtime check during model load (warn if headwise basis L2 diff > 1e-6) 3) run extended eval suite (5k prompts) on staging.

maria: i'll open the issue and attach short reproducer + ci link. tagging @ashok @jin for triage.

ashok: I'll take the loader fix PR. will also run a couple microbenchmarks to ensure no perf regressions.

maria: thanks. small follow-up: we should add a note to onboarding checklist: "verify head-order & per-head rotary scale invariants after conversion and after quantization" :memo:

jin: agreed. adding to onboarding docs.

olga: leaving a TODO to compare int8 quant path as well (maybe less sensitive).

maria: great — closing the loop here, will update thread when PR is up. :thumbsup:
